project_type: Node.js Express API with React frontend (CivicConnect)
build_system: npm scripts - 'npm run dev' for development, 'npm start' for production
test_framework: No test framework configured - manual verification via server startup and API calls
verification_instructions: Start the server with 'node index.js' from the server directory and confirm MongoDB connection succeeds (look for 'Connected to MongoDB' log message)
setup_instructions: Dependencies are already installed at /projects/sandbox/CivicWorld/node_modules. Mongoose 7.7.0 is already in package.json.
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET network mode - full access to MongoDB Atlas cluster. Node.js v22 available via nvm.
contribution_requirements: No CONTRIBUTING.md found. Keep API response shapes identical to existing in-memory implementation for frontend compatibility.
key_patterns: Services are singleton classes exported via module.exports = new ServiceClass(). Controllers call service methods and handle HTTP responses. Auth middleware decodes JWT and sets req.user = { id, email }. The 'id' field in responses uses string IDs (currently Date.now().toString()). Frontend expects fields: id, title, description, category, city, location, imageUrl, reporterId, status, upvoteCount, upvoters, createdAt, updatedAt for issues. For users: id, name, email, city, profilePictureUrl, createdAt, totalPosts, totalUpvotes. For comments: id, issueId, userId, text, createdAt, updatedAt.
directory_structure: server/ - Express backend (index.js entry point), server/src/config/ - DB config, server/src/models/ - Mongoose models (currently placeholder), server/src/services/ - business logic (currently in-memory), server/src/controllers/ - HTTP handlers, server/src/routes/ - Express route definitions, server/src/middleware/ - auth middleware
